statement: For every real H with 1/2<H<1, define rho_0(H)=1 and rho_j(H)=((j+1)^(2H)-2*j^(2H)+|j-1|^(2H))/2 for integers j>=1. For every integer n with 2<=n<=5, let Gamma_n^k(H), 2<=k<=n, be the unique solution of sum_{k=2}^n Gamma_n^k(H)*rho_|l-k|(H)=rho_{l-1}(H), 2<=l<=n. Then all these coefficients are strictly positive. Moreover, for t in (1,2), put T_4(t)=(rho_|i-j|(t/2))_{i,j=1}^4, b_4(t)=(rho_1(t/2),...,rho_4(t/2))^T, and let P(t)=16*det(T_4(t) with column 3 replaced by b_4(t)). The function P(t)/((t-1)*(2-t)^3) extends analytically to [1,2] and is strictly greater than 27/10 there. This subsidiary theorem does not resolve the original all-n claim.
contribution: A rigorous full-H completion of the n=5 one-sided fGn predictor positivity case explicitly identified in Remark 4 of the 2025 primary paper, with an exact rational endpoint-deflated Taylor/Bernstein certificate and a second ball arithmetic interval check. The n<=4 assertion, projection recursion, covariance factorization and approximation tools are not claimed as new. No equivalent n=5 certificate was located in the bounded current primary-source search; priority and mathematical value remain subject to fresh review.
